_comment: Teams under construction. A team is 6 Pokemon; 4 are chosen at preview. A TEAM DOES NOT OWN ITS POKEMON: builds live in builds.json and are reusable across any number of teams - a trained Pokemon is trained, full stop. This file holds only the TEAM-LEVEL decisions: which six, why each one is here, and the items, which the Item Clause makes answerable only once the six are fixed. Never copy a moveset in here for a Pokemon that has a build - reference it and read builds.json. A 'proposed_moves' field is allowed ONLY for a Pokemon that is not yet owned or trained, and is marked as a proposal, not a build. Several Mega Stones on one team are fine - only one Pokemon may Mega Evolve per battle, and that is a per-game choice. Each team carries a 'status' saying whether it is committed or a worked example; read it before assuming the player plays a team listed here.

teams.name: Lightning Rod install
teams.status: REFERENCE / EXERCISE, not a committed team. Built 2026-08-29 as a worked example while the player was testing the teambuilding workflow. Everything in it is verified and it is legal and playable, but the player has NOT said they will run it - do not treat it as their current team or assume the items are locked in.
teams.idea: Jolteon is 200 Speed and Mega Sceptile 197, so Jolteon always moves first. Its Discharge hits All Adjacent Pokemon, which Mega Sceptile's Lightning Rod converts into +1 Sp. Atk with no damage taken, while still chipping both opponents for 80 BP with a 30% paralysis chance each. Sceptile snowballs Sp. Atk every turn for free. The player's opening: turn 1 Sceptile Protect + Jolteon Light Screen (Sceptile is 172 un-mega'd, still slower than Jolteon), then Mega Evolve and attack from turn 2 while Jolteon starts the Discharge chain.

slots.job: Engine. Light Screen, then Discharge every turn. Electroweb for speed control.
slots.item_reason: PLAYER'S DECISION: survive one hit so that at least TWO Discharges happen, which is +2 Sp. Atk on Sceptile. Outranks Light Clay, which would extend Light Screen from 5 turns but does nothing if Jolteon dies first.

slots.job: Win condition. Mega Evolves turn 2, then attacks with a Sp. Atk stack that grows every turn.
slots.item_reason: Mega Stone. The build does not function without it: the Dragon type that makes Dragon Pulse a STAB, 40 Sp. Atk, 25 Speed and Lightning Rod itself all come from the stone.

slots.job: The cover. Resists ALL SIX of Mega Sceptile's weaknesses - Ice, Poison, Flying, Bug, Dragon, Fairy - and it is the only one of the player's 20 builds that does. Good as Gold blanks the status moves that punish a two-turn setup. Nasty Plot behind the same Light Screen is a second win condition if Sceptile falls.
slots.note: Takes Discharge at x1, so it is not a partner for the Discharge turns - it is the other pairing, or the follow-up after Sceptile.
slots.item_reason: The field runs Life Orb 78%, but Smogon ties Life Orb to the FAST spreads and this Gholdengo is the bulky one - 32 HP / 8 Def / 23 SpA / 3 SpD. Life Orb's recoil fights the exact job it has here, which is surviving the Ice and Fairy attacks that Mega Sceptile cannot. Metal Coat takes Make It Rain from 120 to 144 and costs no HP; Smogon notes it OHKOes Mega Aerodactyl. Life Orb stays available if the player would rather have burst than staying power.

slots.job: Protects the setup. Friend Guard cuts 25% off ALL damage the ally takes, which covers the physical side that Light Screen does not. Follow Me pulls single-target attacks off Sceptile, and it does NOT interfere with Discharge because Follow Me only affects single-target moves. Feint breaks a stalling Protect.
slots.item_reason: The field's own top pick at 44%, and the 39% alternative is Focus Sash, which Jolteon has. Exactly right on type: Maushold is pure Normal and takes Fighting at x2, and it has to live long enough to use Follow Me more than once.

slots.job: The Ground answer and a SECOND Discharge engine. Levitate makes it immune to Ground, which is the team's shared hole, without costing a slot to a Pokemon that does nothing else. Its own Discharge feeds Mega Sceptile's Lightning Rod exactly like Jolteon's, so the install survives Jolteon going down. Volt Switch pivots out of a bad matchup instead of losing the turn, and Hydro Pump answers the Ground, Rock and Fire types that come in on the Electric attacks.
slots.note: With Levitate its ONLY weakness is Grass x2 - and Mega Sceptile resists Grass at x0.25, so the two cover each other. Fully special, so Intimidate does nothing to it.
slots.item_reason: 100% of the Worlds Rotom-Wash. It wins the Sitrus over Farigiraf because it is the one that stays on the field taking hits - Levitate leaves it with a single weakness, so recovery compounds - while Farigiraf has a better second option.

slots.job: The two structural answers this team needs, in one slot. TRICK ROOM as a switch (confirmed, see trick_room_rule): the team is 200 / 197 / 131 / 200 and an opposing Trick Room inverts all of it, so Farigiraf turns it back off. ARMOR TAIL blanks Prankster, which answers Whimsicott's Encore - at 23.5% of the ladder, the single worst thing that can land on a two-turn setup. Twin Beam hits twice, so it also breaks Focus Sash.
slots.note: Speed 80, the slowest on the team by a distance, so it also functions if a Trick Room does stay up. Takes Discharge at x1: not a Discharge-turn partner.
slots.item_reason: Only 6% of the field, which runs Sitrus 92% - but Sitrus is on Rotom-Wash, and Colbur answers this team's real hole rather than a generic one. DARK hits Gholdengo x2 and Farigiraf x2, Kingambit is on 52.7% of Worlds teams, and Kowtow Cleave never misses. Colbur halves that hit on the member that has to survive to switch off an opposing Trick Room.

shared_holes.Ground: Jolteon x2, Gholdengo x2. Rotom-Wash and Sceptile are both safe (Levitate; x0.5), so a lead pair can always be built that does not fold to Earthquake, and Jolteon's Focus Sash absorbs one anyway.
shared_holes.Dark: Gholdengo x2, Farigiraf x2. The real one: Kingambit is on 52.7% of Worlds teams and Kowtow Cleave never misses, so Protect is the only hard answer. Maushold's Follow Me and Friend Guard are the mitigation.
shared_holes.Bug: Mega Sceptile x2, Farigiraf x2. Ignorable - no Bug move reaches 1% of ladder usage.
shared_holes.Ice: Mega Sceptile x4 and nothing else now. Gholdengo and Rotom-Wash both resist it. Against a snow team, bench Sceptile.

teams.structural_risk: The team is very fast - 200 / 197 / 131 / 200 - so an opposing Trick Room inverts all of it. The hedge the player owns is Farigiraf, already built with Trick Room, or the slower Kingambit and Scrafty which function better inside someone else's Trick Room.
teams.trick_room_rule: CONFIRMED 2026-08-29. Using Trick Room while Trick Room is active CANCELS it immediately - it is a switch, not a refresh. Three-way agreement: (1) the player's own understanding; (2) champsdex.com, a Champions-specific guide updated 2026-06-14: 'Using Trick Room while your opponent's room is active cancels it immediately'; (3) Bulbapedia for the main series: 'using Trick Room while it is already in effect will end it immediately'. Neither Serebii nor Smogon documents it - Serebii's effect text and in-depth field say only that it gives the field the status for 5 turns, its status-conditions page omits Trick Room entirely, and Smogon says only 'Goes last. For 5 turns, turn order is reversed.' Supporting evidence that Champions did not rebalance the mechanic: priority -7 and 5 turns are identical to the main series. The PP difference (8 here, 5 base in the main series) is NOT a rebalance - Champions rescales PP globally, see the PP note in CLAUDE.md. So Farigiraf's slot is sound: it is a real off switch for an opposing Trick Room.
teams.replaced_aerodactyl: Aerodactyl was cut on the player's call, 2026-08-29: they read it as a Tailwind support, and this team's speed plan is Light Screen plus Electroweb, not Tailwind. Rotom-Wash does the job Aerodactyl was actually there for and does it better: same Ground immunity (Levitate rather than the Flying type), but Aerodactyl was x2 to Ice while Rotom-Wash is x0.5, so the Ice hole drops from two members to one - Mega Sceptile alone. It is also a special attacker, which matches the player's standing preference, and it is a second Lightning Rod feeder. It saves the 2000 VP that Aerodactylite would have cost, so the whole team is now 0 VP. What is lost: Unnerve's Berry shutoff, and Mega Aerodactyl as an alternative win condition in the games where Sceptile is benched.
teams.item_resolution: Item Clause satisfied: six different items, all owned. The one real collision was Sitrus Berry, wanted by Rotom-Wash (100% of the field) and Farigiraf (92%). Rotom-Wash keeps it and Farigiraf takes Colbur, which is the better team-level answer anyway. NOTE: Light Clay is owned and would extend Jolteon's Light Screen from 5 turns, but Jolteon holds Focus Sash by the player's explicit decision - survive first, so that a second Discharge happens at all. Light Clay therefore goes unused by this team; nothing else on it sets a screen.

teams.name: Mega Sol rain
teams.status: SIX SLOTS FILLED but NOT settled - the player is not convinced. Built over a long session 2026-08-30. See open_direction: the player is questioning whether Mega Meganium belongs on a weather team at all. Do not treat this as a committed team.
teams.idea: Mega Meganium's Mega Sol is the only weather-proof ability in the format: it uses its moves as if in harsh sunlight without SETTING sun, so nobody can overwrite it. That lets it live inside the team's own rain, which no other sun option can. Pelipper's Drizzle then does two jobs at once - it turns Archaludon's Electro Shot into an instant 130 BP attack that also gives +1 Sp. Atk per use, and it halves incoming Fire, which is the format's second most common attacking type (10.2%) and the thing Meganium and Gholdengo both fear.
player_rules: No Intimidate anywhere: 7 of the top 8 run Kingambit with Defiant, so leading Intimidate hands it +2 Attack. This is why Incineroar was cut.
Only one support slot. Bring 6 / pick 4 means a second support narrows the options for the four that actually fight.
Special attackers lead; physical is acceptable on secondary slots only.

slots.job: The support slot. Drizzle sets the rain the whole team runs on, plus Tailwind for speed control and Wide Guard against spread moves.
slots.item_reason: PLAYER'S DECISION 2026-08-30, over Damp Rock. Surviving one hit guarantees the rain and the Tailwind actually land; 8 turns of rain is worth nothing if Pelipper dies before setting it.
slots.notes: Hurricane never misses in rain. Smogon flags Wide Guard as the pick over Protect because it blanks Rock Slide from Mega Aerodactyl and Dazzling Gleam from Mega Floette.
slots._proposal: NOT a build - this Pokemon is not owned or trained yet.

slots.job: The wall and the main engine. Electro Shot is instant in rain AND raises its own Sp. Atk by 1 stage every use.
slots.item_reason: 100% of Worlds Archaludon run Leftovers; it is the item the set is designed around.
slots.notes: 10.9% of Worlds teams, Electro Shot on 100% of them, Pelipper as partner on 84%. Weak to Ground x2 - this is half the reason slot 6 must dodge Earthquake.
slots._proposal: NOT a build - this Pokemon is not owned or trained yet.

slots.job: The Mega. A wall that attacks: Weather Ball is a permanent 100 BP Fire move and Synthesis always heals 2/3, both because Mega Sol treats the weather as sun no matter what is actually up.
slots.item_reason: The stone is what creates the form and the ability; without it this is a 525 BST Grass type with nothing.
slots.notes: PLAYER'S SET, and deliberately runs NO Grass attack: Grass is resisted by the six most used Pokemon in the format (Kingambit, Charizard, Incineroar, Sneasler, Venusaur, Whimsicott), so Solar Beam would only hit Basculegion and the rain teams. Dazzling Gleam is the only Fairy attack it learns. Earth Power was considered and rejected - it is the only way to touch Incineroar (41.4%) and Sneasler (26.4%), but it costs Synthesis, which is half of what Mega Sol pays for.
slots.cost: rental - 1 permanence ticket, plus 2000 VP for the stone
slots._proposal: NOT a build - this Pokemon is not owned or trained yet.

slots.job: The Sneasler answer. The ONLY Pokemon in the box that takes zero from both of Sneasler's STABs - Fighting x0 from Ghost, Poison x0 from Steel - and it kills back with Psychic at x4.
slots.item_reason: 78% of Worlds Gholdengo. The set has no boosting move now that Nasty Plot is out, so the damage has to come from the item.
slots.notes: Psychic replaces Nasty Plot, 250 VP. Open question: Power Gem would hit Charizard at x4 (45% of the field) but fitting both it and Psychic costs Make It Rain, its 120 BP spread STAB. Weak to Ground x2 - the other half of the reason slot 6 must dodge Earthquake.
slots.cost: permanent, built - 250 VP for the move swap

slots.job: The sweeper, and it covers three holes in one slot: rain-boosted Water STAB, Fighting x4 into Kingambit (53% of the field), and the team's only Ice.
slots.item_reason: Provisional. Boosts the rain-boosted Aqua Step it clicks most; revisit once slot 6 is settled.
slots.notes: PLAYER'S PICK. Aqua Step gives +1 Speed per use and Moxie gives +1 Attack per KO, so it snowballs from base 85 Speed. Triple Axel over Ice Spinner is the player's call: 20+40+60 = 120 total vs 80, and being multi-hit it breaks Focus Sash, the format's most contested item at 339 Worlds teams. Also learns Rain Dance, so it can re-set the rain if Pelipper is gone. Physical, so Intimidate hurts it - but Aqua Step and Moxie out-scale Intimidate.
slots._proposal: NOT a build - this Pokemon is not owned or trained yet.

slots.job: The glue. Rage Powder pulls Sneasler's Close Combat and Dire Claw off Archaludon and Meganium, Hospitality heals the partner 25% on entry, and Life Dew tops the whole side up.
slots.item_reason: Smogon: Colbur lets Sinistcha take a Kowtow Cleave from half HP instead of needing to be at full, so it can safely Rage Powder in FRONT of Kingambit and nullify Sucker Punch. Kingambit is on 53% of the field and 7 of the top 8, so that is the single most valuable thing this slot can do.
slots.notes: PLAYER'S PICK 2026-08-30, chosen for the ability rather than the stats. Smogon names Sinistcha by name as the ideal partner for BOTH fixed pieces: for Archaludon 'maximum support through Life Dew and Hospitality recovery, Rage Powder redirection', and for Gholdengo 'can heal up Gholdengo with Hospitality and redirect many attacks'. Three specific fits with this team: (1) Meganium is Poison x4 and Sinistcha redirects Sneasler's Dire Claw and Gunk Shot away from it; (2) Quaquaval snowballs with Aqua Step and Moxie, and Smogon notes boosting Pokemon 'make excellent use of Sinistcha's redirection and Hospitality'; (3) Sinistcha's own worst check is Mega Charizard Y's sun-boosted Heat Wave, which ignores Rage Powder and OHKOes it - and Pelipper's rain is exactly what neuters it. Smogon: 'Pelipper and Politoed effectively neuter Sinistcha's biggest check in Mega Charizard Y.' PROTECT, NOT TRICK ROOM: Smogon says to drop Trick Room when the team already has speed control, and Pelipper's Tailwind is it. Defensively it also answers the Ground question indirectly - Grass/Ghost is Ground x0.5 and immune to Fighting and Normal.
slots.cost: rental - 1 permanence ticket, then a build

shared_holes.Fire: Meganium x2 and Gholdengo x2, but the team's own rain halves it. The real risk is losing the weather war to Charizard-Y's Drought, on 45% of the field.
shared_holes.Electric: Pelipper x4 and Quaquaval x2, but the format barely uses it - 2 attacking Electric moves in the whole top 8, 1.5% of the field.
shared_holes.Rock: No Rock attack on the team, so Charizard-Y (45%) is hit at x2 instead of x4. Gholdengo's Power Gem is the fix if it is ever needed.

weather_control.why_it_matters: 65.7% of Worlds teams carry a weather setter that is not rain, so two thirds of the field can switch this team's engine off. Sun alone is 48%.

who_sets_it.Mega Charizard Y: Drought, 45.2% of teams. Heat Wave 100%, Weather Ball 98%, Ancient Power 55%, Solar Beam 31%. Modest on 114 of 178, so many are not max Speed.
who_sets_it.Politoed: Drizzle, 2.3% - this one is fine, it sets OUR weather

weather_control.the_key_finding: ROCK hits four of the five setters: Charizard-Y x4, Froslass x2, Ninetales-Alola x2, Torkoal x2. The fifth, Tyranitar, is Fighting x4 - which Quaquaval's Close Combat already covers.
weather_control.no_way_to_opt_out: Champions has no Utility Umbrella, and Cloud Nine exists only on Altaria and Drampa, neither of which the player owns. The weather war has to be won, not dodged.
weather_control.who_actually_suffers: Only Archaludon and Pelipper. Archaludon is the real casualty - without rain, Electro Shot stops being instant and becomes a two-turn move, which is useless in doubles. Mega Meganium does not care at all: Mega Sol gives it sun regardless.
weather_control.aerodactyl_option: Speed 130 -> max+ 200, beats Charizard-Y's 167 with no Tailwind needed. Resists Fire x0.5. Rock Slide is x4 AND All Adjacent Foes. Learns Rain Dance and Tailwind, so it doubles as a weather reset and a backup speed setter. Already built at 66/66 with Rock Slide / Protect / Tailwind / Dual Wingbeat - only Rain Dance over Dual Wingbeat would be worth 250 VP. Would come in for Gholdengo, whose Sneasler job is already covered twice over by Sinistcha's Rage Powder and Pelipper's Hurricane.

rejected_and_why.Lycanroc with Accelerock: The right idea - priority +1 Rock hits Charizard-Y x4 regardless of Speed - but the player does not own Lycanroc, and Accelerock is learnable ONLY by Lycanroc and Lycanroc-Dusk in the whole format. Encounter-only.
rejected_and_why.Power Gem on Gholdengo: Withdrawn. Charizard-Y at max+ 167 outspeeds Gholdengo's 149 and hits it with a sun-boosted Heat Wave at x2, so Power Gem only ever fires under Tailwind or as a revenge kill.
rejected_and_why.Meteor Beam on Archaludon: 120 BP special Rock at x4 looks ideal, but Power Herb does not exist in Champions, so it always charges. Useless in doubles.
rejected_and_why.Maushold: Second support. With bring 6 / pick 4 a second support narrows the four that actually fight.
rejected_and_why.Rotom-Wash: Recommended on a wrong claim - it takes Electric at x1, not x0.5, because Water cancels the Electric resistance.
rejected_and_why.Incineroar: Intimidate feeds Kingambit's Defiant, and 7 of the top 8 run Kingambit.

teams.open_direction: PLAYER, 2026-08-30, not yet resolved: 'maybe Mega Meganium should not fight over weather at all and should just concentrate on surviving, with different partners.' This is the real fork. Mega Sol makes Meganium weather-independent, so pairing it with a rain core drags it into a war it does not need to fight - while Archaludon is the opposite, it LIVES on the rain. The two pull apart. Either build the rain team and accept Meganium is a passenger that happens to be immune to the downside, or build around Meganium as a weather-proof bulky attacker and drop the rain engine, which means Archaludon loses most of its appeal.

teams.idea: Trick Room instead of weather. Mega Sol already makes Meganium weather-proof, so a weather core dragged it into a war it had no stake in - and 65.7% of the field can set a weather that is not rain. Trick Room cannot be overwritten by Drought, Sand Stream or Snow Warning, and it suits Meganium's actual shape: 115/115 defences, Synthesis at 2/3, Weather Ball at a permanent 100 BP Fire. It rewards bulky and slow, which is what Meganium is; Tailwind rewards fast and frail, which it is not.
player_rules_learned_this_session: ONE support slot only. With bring 6 / pick 4, two supports leave only two attackers - 'llevar 2 soportes a 2v2 es horrible'. Farigiraf is the support; do not propose a second Trick Room setter or a second redirector.

Kingambit is the EXCEPTION to the Intimidate rule - Defiant turns an opposing Intimidate into +2 Attack, so it is never 'exposed' to Intimidate. Do not count it among physical attackers that Intimidate punishes.
With Kingambit and Tyranitar on the same team a Ghost type is close to mandatory: both are Dark-types with a Fighting x4 weakness, and Ghost is immune to Fighting.

Do not recommend a Pokemon whose value came from its Mega when the Mega slot is taken - base Eelektross is a weak Pokemon and its Giga Drain / Flamethrower coverage is already done better by Meganium.
Every slot needs a job. 'It is slow so it fits Trick Room' is not a reason - Hatterene was rejected on exactly that.

All eight are 100% Mega, 100% Quiet, 100% Cameruptite, and 7 of 8 share the identical moveset PROTECT / EARTH POWER / HEAT WAVE / ANCIENT POWER (the eighth swaps Heat Wave for Eruption). So a Farigiraf Trick Room team is not merely A home for Mega Camerupt, it is the ONLY home anyone has found. ANCIENT POWER on 8/8 is the detail to keep: Fire/Ground cannot touch Flying, and Rock is x4 on Mega Charizard Y and x2 on Aerodactyl, Staraptor and Pelipper. Sheer Force strips its 10% omniboost and adds 30% power instead. The field's shell is Camerupt + Farigiraf + Kingambit (4/6) + Sylveon/Kangaskhan (3/6 each); none ran Chesnaught. NOTE the teamlists say ability 'Solid Rock' - that is the BASE ability, correct per CLAUDE.md, and it becomes Sheer Force on Mega Evolution. THIS TEAM IS ARGUABLY A BETTER HOME THAN THE WORLDS ONES: Camerupt's one fatal weakness is Water x4 (Basculegion Wave Crash 185-219%, Mega Swampert 231-271%), and this team carries Primarina and Chesnaught, both Water x0.5. Most of the six Worlds teams carried no Water answer at all.
unconstrained_design_2026_09_06.heracross_measured_and_it_does_NOT_fit_t: Player asked 2026-09-06 whether Mega Heracross belongs here. Measured, and the answer is no - but not for the usual reason. OFFENSIVELY IT IS THE BEST ANSWER ON THE BOARD: with Skill Link (5 hits, accuracy rolled once), Pin Missile OHKOes the Farigiraf mirror at 115.9-139.1% and Bullet Seed OHKOes Mega Swampert at 121.9-147.6% - it solves BOTH remaining walls single-handed, and Close Combat does 263-310% to Kingambit. Mega Heracross is Atk 185 / Def 115 / SpD 105, Spe 75. AND IT IS FREE: Heracronite is already owned and Heracross is in home_box x2, so it costs 0 VP where Cameruptite costs 2000. THE DISQUALIFIER IS THE ROTATION TEST THE PLAYER THEMSELVES APPLIED: Bug/Fighting is Flying x4, exactly like Chesnaught's Grass/Fighting. Mega Staraptor Brave Bird 186-220%, Mega Charizard Y Hurricane 199-237%, Mega Aerodactyl Dual Wingbeat 120-146% - all guaranteed OHKOs on both. Chesnaught and Heracross are bad in the SAME games, so as a second Mega it buys no matchup flexibility; Camerupt does (12 of the top 20 favour it where Chesnaught folds). Heracross is a REPLACEMENT candidate for Chesnaught, not a complement, and it belongs on a team where something else answers Flying. Worlds: 0 of 645 teams across all three divisions ran it; ladder 0.1%.

why_slot_6_is_KINGAMBIT.the_other_hole_is_defensive: Scanning the top 15 against the five, there is NO member that resists both types of Kingambit (52.8%), Mega Charizard Y (45.2%), Garchomp (38.3%), Basculegion (34.0%), Sinistcha (22.6%) or Mega Delphox (11.7%). KINGAMBIT TOPS IT: it resists 5 of the 8 attacking types involved and is the only safe switch into the format's #1 Pokemon, the Kingambit mirror.
why_slot_6_is_KINGAMBIT.and_it_closes_the_last_wall: Kowtow Cleave is a GUARANTEED OHKO on the Farigiraf mirror (101.4-119.8%) and it NEVER MISSES - accuracy 101 in the Champions movedex. Iron Head guarantees Mega Floette (104.3-124.2%). It takes the Kingambit mirror's own Kowtow Cleave at 15.5-18.4%, Basculegion Wave Crash at 37.7-44.9% and Garchomp Earthquake at 52.2-61.8%.
why_slot_6_is_KINGAMBIT.it_is_already_built: Defiant, Adamant, 32 HP / 32 Atk / 2 Def, Kowtow Cleave / Sucker Punch / Iron Head / Protect. Mega Staraptor Close Combat 179.7-210.6% and Sneasler Close Combat 168.1-199.0% are guaranteed OHKOs on it. THUNDER PUNCH is a guaranteed OHKO on Pelipper (111.6-133.3%) with no drawback at all - Supercell Slam hits harder (149.7-176.9%) but costs 50% max HP on a 5% miss, and Wild Charge (133.3-157.8%) carries 1/4 recoil, so the weakest of the three is the right one. Heavy Slam OHKOes Alolan Ninetales (202.5-240.0%). Defensively at 32 HP / 32 Def with THICK FAT it is the only candidate that survives EITHER of Mega Staraptor's moves: Close Combat 83.1-98.9% and Brave Bird 41.6-49.4%. (Kingambit dies to Close Combat at 146.9-173.9%; Empoleon is an 88% OHKO roll.) Sneasler Close Combat 79.4-94.4%. Charizard Y Heat Wave is 10.1-12.4%, which closes the Fire hole Chesnaught and Gholdengo share. Kingambit Kowtow Cleave 28.5-34.1%, Basculegion Wave Crash 36.0-42.7%, Pelipper Hurricane 21.3-25.1%. ITS COST: Crunch only 2HKOes the Farigiraf mirror (55.1-65.7%), so the last offensive wall stays a 2HKO instead of becoming an OHKO. Camerupt's Heat Wave already 2HKOs that mirror, so nothing is lost that the team did not already have.
SLOT_6_REOPENED_2026_09_06.EMPOLEON_the_Competitive_option: OWNED, Spe 60, SpA 111. Ice Beam is a guaranteed OHKO on Garchomp (108.7-129.2%) and Water/Steel resists Water, which makes it the best pure RAIN BODY of the three: in rain it takes Basculegion Wave Crash as a guaranteed 3HKO and Pelipper Hurricane as a 5HKO. BUT it does not KO Pelipper itself (Ice Beam 42.2-49.7%), has no answer to the Farigiraf mirror (Throat Chop 47.3-56.0% and it is physical off the wrong stat), and it is Ground x2, which would make THREE of the six weak to Earthquake alongside Gholdengo and Camerupt - the player's own standing objection.
SLOT_6_REOPENED_2026_09_06.verdict: Snorlax on the numbers; Empoleon if the player wants the Competitive ability and the harder rain wall; Kingambit only if the Farigiraf-mirror OHKO is judged worth more than the Pelipper answer. NOT DECIDED - the player's call.
SLOT_6_REOPENED_2026_09_06.CORRECTION_the_Fighting_axis_2026_09_06: CAUGHT BY THE PLAYER. An earlier line here said Close Combat 'deletes Chesnaught and Kingambit'. THAT IS WRONG ABOUT CHESNAUGHT: Grass/Fighting takes Fighting at x1, and Mega Chesnaught's Def 172 turns that into only 29.7-35.9% from Mega Staraptor's Close Combat. What deletes Chesnaught is BRAVE BIRD - Flying x4, 119.0-143.6% - exactly as its own build's threats field already said. THE TWO ARE OPPOSITE, not alike: Chesnaught is Fighting x1 / FLYING x4, Kingambit is FIGHTING x4 / Flying x0.5. Mega Staraptor beats both, but with a different move each time, and it picks the move after seeing which one is out. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS DECISION, AND IT FAVOURS KINGAMBIT: Kingambit RESISTS Flying at x0.5 and takes Brave Bird for 18.4-21.7%, so it is a real Brave Bird switch-in for Chesnaught's x4 hole - the only other one on the team is Gholdengo. That merit was understated. Snorlax is Flying x1 (41.6-49.4%), Empoleon x0.5 (24.1-28.8%).
